source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse tells a patient, 'I'll restrain you if you don't take your medicine.' This is:
questions.rationale: Assault is a threat of harmful contact; battery is actual unconsented touching.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Assault (PDF p. 503)
questions.quote: A nurse threatens to restrain patient if he will not take his medicine.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse gives an injection after the patient refused it. The nurse may be charged with:
questions.rationale: Battery is intentional unconsented physical touching.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Battery (PDF p. 503)
questions.quote: When a patient refuses an injection and the nurse gives it anyway

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A competent patient insists on leaving against advice. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Detaining him is false imprisonment; explain consequences and allow discharge against advice.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, False Imprisonment (PDF p. 503)
questions.quote: he is allowed to go home against advice

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Closing the curtains during a physical examination protects the patient's:
questions.rationale: Privacy relates to the person; confidentiality relates to information.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Right to Privacy (PDF p. 503)
questions.quote: Curtains are closed during physical examination

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse posts false, damaging written statements about a colleague. This is:
questions.rationale: Libel is written defamation; slander is spoken; a third party must receive it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Defamation (PDF p. 503)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Under the Revised Penal Code, a felony is frustrated when the offender:
questions.rationale: Frustrated: all acts performed but not produced for reasons independent of the offender.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Felony Degrees (PDF p. 503)
questions.quote: Did not produce felony by reason of causes independent of the will of the perpetrator

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A person who knows of a crime and later helps the offender escape is an:
questions.rationale: Accessories act after the crime; accomplices cooperate before or during.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Conspiracy (PDF p. 503)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Self-defense with all its elements present is a:
questions.rationale: Justifying: no liability; incomplete self-defense becomes mitigating.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Justifying Circumstance (PDF p. 504)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Voluntary surrender to authorities is which type of circumstance?
questions.rationale: Mitigating circumstances reduce liability (voluntary surrender, confession).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mitigating Circumstance (PDF p. 504)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Looting during a calamity is which type of circumstance?
questions.rationale: Crimes in times of calamity, cruelty, treachery, and premeditation increase liability.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Aggravating Circumstance (PDF p. 504)
questions.quote: Crimes in times of calamity (Looting, profiteering)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which law is the Magna Carta for Public Health Workers?
questions.rationale: RA 7305; RA 7160 is Local Government Code; RA 6713 ethics of officials; RA 7875 PhilHealth.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Laws Related to Nursing (PDF p. 505)
questions.quote: Magna Carta for Public Health Workers

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which law mandates rooming-in and breastfeeding in health facilities?
questions.rationale: RA 7600 (Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Act, amended by RA 10028).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Laws Related to Nursing (PDF p. 505)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The Generics Act of the Philippines is:
questions.rationale: RA 6675 Generics Act; RA 7719 Blood Services; RA 9262 VAWC; RA 8749 Clean Air Act.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Laws Related to Nursing (PDF p. 505)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which law governs the National Blood Services program?
questions.rationale: RA 7719 promotes voluntary blood donation and safe blood supply.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Laws Related to Nursing (PDF p. 505)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which theory holds that leaders are born, not made?
questions.rationale: Great man/trait theory: inborn characteristics make leaders.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Leadership Theories (PDF p. 506)
questions.quote: Great leaders are born and not made.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A head nurse inspires staff, promotes their development, and encourages creativity. This is:
questions.rationale: Transformational leaders inspire and develop followers; transactional uses rewards and punishment.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Transformational Theory (PDF p. 506)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Fiedler's contingency theory considers leader-member relations, task structure, and:
questions.rationale: Fiedler: leader-member relations, task structure, position power.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Contingency Theory (PDF p. 506)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During a code, which leadership style is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Emergencies need quick decisions and strong control.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Leadership Styles (PDF p. 507)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Laissez-faire leadership works best with staff who are:
questions.rationale: Little control requires self-directed, skilled members.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Leadership Styles (PDF p. 507)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Who is the Father of Scientific Management?
questions.rationale: Taylor used stopwatch studies; Fayol: management process; Weber: organization/bureaucracy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Management Theories (PDF p. 507)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: According to Herzberg, which is a motivator rather than a hygiene factor?
questions.rationale: Motivators: achievement, recognition, responsibility, growth; hygiene: policy, supervision, conditions.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Herzberg (PDF p. 508)
questions.quote: Motivators or satisfiers identified were achievement, recognition

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A manager believing staff dislike work and must be threatened follows:
questions.rationale: McGregor's Theory X assumes people avoid work; Theory Y assumes self-direction.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, McGregor (PDF p. 508)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Staff follow a senior nurse because they admire her and want to be like her. This is:
questions.rationale: Referent power comes from admiration and identification.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sources of Power (PDF p. 508)
questions.quote: Leader is admired and exerts influence because the followers desire to be like the leader

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Influence based on being the mayor's daughter reflects which power?
questions.rationale: Connection power comes from links to influential people.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sources of Power (PDF p. 509)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The Pareto principle states that:
questions.rationale: The 80-20 rule: focus on the vital few causes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Principles of Management (PDF p. 509)
questions.quote: Roughly 80% of the effects comes from 20% of the causes

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A head nurse is an example of which management level?
questions.rationale: Head nurse: first level; supervisor: middle; chief nurse: top.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Management Levels (PDF p. 510)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Strategic planning typically covers:
questions.rationale: Strategic planning sets overall goals for 3–5 years by top managers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Planning (PDF p. 510)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A brief statement of why an organization exists is its:
questions.rationale: Mission: reason for existence; vision: future; philosophy: values.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Planning (PDF p. 510)
questions.quote: It is a brief statement identifying the reason why an organization exists.
